Integral representations for solutions of exponential Gauß-Manin systems

Marco Hien Address: Marco Hien
NWF I – Mathematik
Universität Regensburg
93040 Regensburg
Germany Email address: marco.hien@mathematik.uni-regensburg.de and Celine Roucairol Address: Celine Roucairol
Lehrstuhl für Mathematik VI
Universität Mannheim
A5 6
68161 Mannheim
Germany Email address: celine.roucairol@uni-mannheim.de
Abstract.

Let f,g:U→𝔸1f,g:U\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} be two algebraically independent regular functions from the smooth affine complex variety UU to the affine line. The associated exponential Gauß-Manin systems on the affine line are defined to be the cohomology sheaves of the direct image of the exponential differential system 𝒪U​eg\mathcal{O}_{U}e^{g} with respect to ff. We prove that its holomorphic solutions admit representations in terms of period integrals over topological chains with possibly closed support and with rapid decay condition.

Key words and phrases: 
Gauß-Manin systems, 𝒟\mathcal{D}-modules
1991 Mathematics Subject Classification
32S40, 32C38, 14F40

1. Introduction

Let UU be a smooth affine complex variety of dimension nn and let f,g:U→𝔸1f,g:U\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} be two regular functions which we assume to be algebraically independent. We consider the flat algebraic connection ∇:𝒪U⟶ΩU1\nabla:\mathcal{O}_{U}\longrightarrow\Omega^{1}_{U} on the trivial line bundle 𝒪U\mathcal{O}_{U} defined as ∇u=d​u+d​g⋅u\nabla u=du+dg\cdot u. Let us denote the associated holonomic 𝒟U\mathcal{D}_{U}-module by 𝒪U​eg\mathcal{O}_{U}e^{g}, i.e. the trivial 𝒪U\mathcal{O}_{U}-module on which any vector field ξ\xi on UU acts via the associated derivation ∇ξ\nabla_{\xi} induced by the connection. Let 𝒩\mathcal{N} be the direct image 𝒩:=f+​(𝒪U​eg)\mathcal{N}:=f_{+}(\mathcal{O}_{U}e^{g}) in the theory of 𝒟\mathcal{D}-modules (see e.g. [2]). Then 𝒩\mathcal{N} is a complex of 𝒟𝔸1\mathcal{D}_{{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}-modules and we consider its kk-th cohomology sheaf

ℋk​f+​(𝒪U​eg),\mathcal{H}^{k}f_{+}(\mathcal{O}_{U}e^{g})\ ,

a holonomic 𝒟𝔸1\mathcal{D}_{{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}-module.

There is an alternative point of view of ℋk​𝒩\mathcal{H}^{k}\mathcal{N} in terms of flat connections: outside a finite subset Σ1⊂𝔸1\Sigma_{1}\subset{\mathbb{A}}^{1}, the 𝒪𝔸1\mathcal{O}_{{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}-module ℋk​f+​(𝒪U​eg)\mathcal{H}^{k}f_{+}(\mathcal{O}_{U}e^{g}) is locally free, hence a flat connection. This connections coincides with the Gauß-Manin connection on the relative de Rham cohomology

ℋk​(𝒩)|𝔸1∖Σ1≅(𝑹k+n−1​f∗​(ΩU|𝔸1⋅,∇),∇G​M)|𝔸1∖Σ1,\mathcal{H}^{k}(\mathcal{N})|_{{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\smallsetminus\Sigma_{1}}\cong\big(\boldsymbol{R}^{k+n-1}f_{\ast}(\Omega_{U|{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}^{\raisebox{-0.90417pt}{\mbox{\boldmath$\cdot$}}},\nabla),\nabla_{GM}\big)|_{{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\smallsetminus\Sigma_{1}}\ ,

i.e. the corresponding higher direct image of the complex of relative differential forms on UU with respect to ff and the differential induced by the absolute connection, as in [6]. It is a flat connection over 𝔸1∖Σ1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\smallsetminus\Sigma_{1}.

In the case g=0g=0, which is classically called the Gauß-Manin system of ff, it is well-known that the solutions admit integral representations (see [10] and [12]). The aim of the present article is to give such a description of the solutions in the more general case of the Gauß-Manin system of the exponential module 𝒪U​eg\mathcal{O}_{U}e^{g}, which we will call exponential Gauß-Manin system. A major difficulty lies in the definition of the integration involved. In the case of vanishing gg, the connection is regular singular at infinity and the topological cycles over which the integrations are performed can be chosen with compact support inside the affine variety UU. In the exponential case g≠0g\neq 0, the connection is irregular singular at infinity and we will have to consider integration paths approaching the irregular locus at infinity.

A systematic examination of period integrals in more general irregular singular situations over complex surfaces has been carried out in [5] resulting in a perfect dualtiy between the de Rham cohomology and some homology groups, the rapid decay homology groups, in terms of period integrals. We will prove in this article that this result generalizes to arbitrary dimension in case of an elementary exponential connection 𝒪​eg\mathcal{O}e^{g} as before, see Theorem 2.4.

With this tool at hand, we construct a local system Hkr​d~\widetilde{H^{rd}_{k}} on 𝔸1∖Σ2{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\smallsetminus\Sigma_{2}, the stalk at point tt of which is the rapid decay homology Hkr​d​(f−1​(t),e−gt)H^{rd}_{k}(f^{-1}(t),e^{-g_{t}}) of the restriction of 𝒪U​e−g\mathcal{O}_{U}e^{-g} to the fibre f−1​(t)f^{-1}(t). The set Σ2\Sigma_{2} can be described using a compactification (F,G):X→ℙ1×ℙ1(F,G):X\to\mathbb{P}^{1}\times\mathbb{P}^{1} of the map (f,g):U→𝔸1×𝔸1(f,g):U\to\mathbb{A}^{1}\times\mathbb{A}^{1} (see Proposition 3.5). Let Δ¯\overline{\Delta} be the projective variety in ℙ1×ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1}\times\mathbb{P}^{1} such that (F,G)(F,G) is a locally trivial fibration out of Δ¯\overline{\Delta}. The set Σ2\Sigma_{2} can be choosen as the set of t0∈𝔸1t_{0}\in\mathbb{A}^{1} such that (t0,∞)(t_{0},\infty) belongs to the closure of Δ¯∖(ℙ1×{∞})\overline{\Delta}\setminus(\mathbb{P}^{1}\times\{\infty\}) in ℙ1×ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1}\times\mathbb{P}^{1}.

Let Σ=Σ1∪Σ2\Sigma=\Sigma_{1}\cup\Sigma_{2}. We prove that given a flat section ct⊗egtc_{t}\otimes e^{g_{t}} in the local system Hk+n−1r​dH^{rd}_{k+n-1} and a relative differential form ω\omega in Ωr​e​lk+n−1​(f−1​(𝔸1∖Σ))\Omega_{rel}^{k+n-1}(f^{-1}({\mathbb{A}}^{1}\smallsetminus\Sigma)) (which describes the analytification of ℋk​𝒩\mathcal{H}^{k}\mathcal{N}, see Proposition 3.4), the integral

(1.1) ∫ctω|f−1​(t)⋅egt\int_{c_{t}}\omega|_{f^{-1}(t)}\cdot e^{g_{t}}

gives a (multivalued) holomorphic solution of the exponential Gauß-Manin system. As a consequence of the duality proved in Theorem 2.4, we deduce that all (multivalued) holomorphic solutions on 𝔸1∖Σ{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\smallsetminus\Sigma can be obtained by this construction, i.e. we achieve the following theorem (Theorem 3.7) which is the main result of this article:

Theorem 1.1.

For any simply connected open subset V⊂ℂ∖ΣV\subset{\mathbb{C}}\smallsetminus\Sigma, the space of holomorphic solutions of the exponential Gauß-Manin system ℋk​𝒩\mathcal{H}^{k}\mathcal{N} is isomorphic to the space of flat sections in the local system Hk+n−1r​d~\widetilde{H^{rd}_{k+n-1}} over VV.

The isomorphism in the theorem is given in terms of the integration (1.1). We want to remark that this theorem generalizes similar results by F. Pham for the Fourier-Laplace transform of the Gauß-Manin systems of a regular function h:U→𝔸1h:U\to\mathbb{A}^{1} (consider f:𝔸1×U→𝔸1f:\mathbb{A}^{1}\times U\to\mathbb{A}^{1} to be the first canonical projection and g:𝔸1×U→𝔸1g:\mathbb{A}^{1}\times U\to\mathbb{A}^{1} given by g⁡(x,u)=x​h​(u)g(x,u)=xh(u), cf. [11]). It also includes other well-known examples as the integral representations of the Bessel-functions for instance (cf. the introduction of [1]).

2. The period pairing

Consider the situation described in the introduction, namely f,g:U→𝔸1f,g:U\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} being two algebraically independent regular functions on the smooth affine complex variety UU. The main result of this work is to give a representation of the Gauß-Manin solutions in terms of period integrals. The proof relies on a duality statement between the algebraic de Rham cohomology of the exponential connection associated to gg and some Betti homology groups with decay condition. The present section is devoted to the proof of this duality statement, which is a generalization of the analogous result for surfaces in [5] to the case of exponential line bundles in arbitrary dimensions.

2.1. Definition

Let us start with any smooth affine complex variety UtU_{t} and a regular function gt:Ut→𝔸1g_{t}:U_{t}\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. Note, that the index tt is irrelevant in this section but will become meaningful later in the application to the Gauß-Manin system where UtU_{t} will denote the smooth fibres f−1​(t)f^{-1}(t).

We assume that UtU_{t} is embedded into a smooth projective variety XtX_{t} with the complement Dt:=Xt∖UtD_{t}:=X_{t}\smallsetminus U_{t} being a divisor with normal crossings. Moreover, we require that gtg_{t} extends to a meromorphic mapping on XtX_{t}. In particular, if y∈Dty\in D_{t} is a point at infinity, we can choose coordinates x1,…,xnx_{1},\ldots,x_{n} of XtX_{t} centered at yy such that locally Dt={x1⋯xk=0}D_{t}=\{x_{1}\cdots x_{k}=0\} for some k∈{1,…,n}k\in\{1,\ldots,n\} and such that we have

gt(x)=x1n1⋯xrnr⋅u(x)g_{t}(x)=x_{1}^{n_{1}}\cdots x_{r}^{n_{r}}\cdot u(x)

locally at yy, where r≤kr\leq k and the exponents ni∈ℤn_{i}\in{\mathbb{Z}} are either all positive or all negative and uu is holomorphic and non-vanishing on DtD_{t} (i.e. gtg_{t} will not have indeterminancies at DtD_{t}).

The function gtg_{t} defines a flat meromorphic connection ∇t\nabla_{t} of exponential type on UtU_{t}, denoted 𝒪​egt\mathcal{O}e^{g_{t}} on the trivial line bundle 𝒪Ut\mathcal{O}_{U_{t}} with connection defined as

∇t1=d​gt∈ΩUt|ℂ1.\nabla_{t}1=dg_{t}\in\Omega^{1}_{U_{t}|{\mathbb{C}}}\ .

In [5], a duality pairing between the de Rham cohomology of a flat meromorphic connection (admitting a good formal structure) and a certain homology theory, the rapid decay homology, is constructed in the case dim(Xt)=2\dim(X_{t})=2, generalizing previous constructions of Bloch and Esnault for curves. For connections of exponential type lying in the main focus of this work, we will now generalized these results to the case of arbitrary dimension. We remark that a crucial point in [5] is to work with a good compactification with respect to the given vector bundle and connection which is always fulfilled for the connections of exponential type considered above.

We recall the definition of rapid decay homology as in [5]. Consider the real oriented blow-up π:Xt~→Xtan\pi:\widetilde{X_{t}}\to X^{\rm an}_{t} of the irreducible components of DtD_{t} (cp. [9]). Let 𝒞Xt~−p\mathcal{C}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{-p} denote the sheaf associated to the presheaf V↦Sp​(Xt~,Xt~∖V)V\mapsto S_{p}(\widetilde{X_{t}},\widetilde{X_{t}}\smallsetminus V) of ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-vector spaces, where Sp​(Y)S_{p}(Y) denotes the groups of piecewise smooth singular pp-chains in YY and Sp​(Y,A)S_{p}(Y,A) the relative chains for a pair of topological spaces A⊂YA\subset Y.

We adopt the standard sign convention for the resulting complex 𝒞Xt~−⁣⋅\mathcal{C}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{-\raisebox{-0.90417pt}{\mbox{\boldmath$\cdot$}}}. i.e. the differential of 𝒞Xt~−⁣⋅\mathcal{C}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{-\raisebox{-0.90417pt}{\mbox{\boldmath$\cdot$}}} will be given by (−1)r(-1)^{r} times the topological boundary operator ∂\partial on 𝒞Xt~−r\mathcal{C}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{-r}. If d:=dimℂ(Xt)d:=\dim_{\mathbb{C}}(X_{t}), the complex 𝒞Xt~−⁣⋅\mathcal{C}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{-\raisebox{-0.90417pt}{\mbox{\boldmath$\cdot$}}} is a resolution of the sheaf ȷ~!ℂUtan[2d]\widetilde{\jmath}_{!}{\mathbb{C}}_{U_{t}^{\rm an}}[2d] which in turn is the dualizing sheaf on the compact real manifold Xt~\widetilde{X_{t}} with boundary Dt~=Xt~∖Utan\widetilde{D_{t}}=\widetilde{X_{t}}\smallsetminus U_{t}^{\rm an} (cp. [19]).

Now, let 𝒞Xt~,Dt~−⁣⋅\mathcal{C}_{\widetilde{X_{t}},\widetilde{D_{t}}}^{-\raisebox{-0.90417pt}{\mbox{\boldmath$\cdot$}}} be the complex of chains relative to the boundary Dt~\widetilde{D_{t}}, i.e. the sheaf associated to

V↦S⋅​(Xt~,(Xt~∖V)∪Dt~).V\mapsto S_{\raisebox{-0.90417pt}{\mbox{\boldmath$\cdot$}}}(\widetilde{X_{t}},(\widetilde{X_{t}}\smallsetminus V)\cup\widetilde{D_{t}})\ .

Let c∈Γ⁡(V,𝒞Xt~,Dt~−⁣⋅)c\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal{C}_{\widetilde{X_{t}},\widetilde{D_{t}}}^{-\raisebox{-0.90417pt}{\mbox{\boldmath$\cdot$}}}) be a local section over some open V⊂Xt~V\subset\widetilde{X_{t}}, represented by a piecewise smooth map from the standard pp-simplex Δp\Delta^{p} to Xt~\widetilde{X_{t}}. We consider cc always together with the solution egte^{g_{t}} of the dual of the given connection of exponential type and will therefore write c⊗egtc\otimes e^{g_{t}} for cc in the following definition (in the terminology of [5], we consider c⊗egtc\otimes e^{g_{t}} as a section in 𝒞Xt~,Dt~−⁣⋅⊗ℚȷ~∗​ℰ\mathcal{C}_{\widetilde{X_{t}},\widetilde{D_{t}}}^{-\raisebox{-0.90417pt}{\mbox{\boldmath$\cdot$}}}\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}}\widetilde{\jmath}_{\ast}\mathcal{E} where ℰ\mathcal{E} denoted the local system associated to the dual bundle 𝒪Ut​e−gt\mathcal{O}_{U_{t}}e^{-g_{t}}, in our case the trivial system with basis egte^{g_{t}}).

Now, consider a point y∈c⁡(Δp)∩Dt~∩Vy\in c(\Delta^{p})\cap\widetilde{D_{t}}\cap V. Choose local coordinates x1,…,xdx_{1},\ldots,x_{d} of XtX_{t} around y=0y=0 such that Dt={x1⋯xk=0}D_{t}=\{x_{1}\cdots x_{k}=0\}.

Definition 2.1.

We call c⊗egtc\otimes e^{g_{t}} a rapid decay chain, if for all yy as above, the function egt​(x)e^{g_{t}(x)} has rapid decay for the argument approaching Dt~\widetilde{D_{t}}, i.e. if for all N∈ℕkN\in{\mathbb{N}}^{k} there is a CN>0C_{N}>0 such that

|egt​(x)|≤CN⋅|x1|N1⋯|xk|Nk|e^{g_{t}(x)}|\leq C_{N}\cdot|x_{1}|^{N_{1}}\cdots|x_{k}|^{N_{k}}

for all x∈(c⁡(Δp)∖Dt~)∩Vx\in(c(\Delta^{p})\!\smallsetminus\!\widetilde{D_{t}})\cap V with small |x1|,…,|xk||x_{1}|,\ldots,|x_{k}|.

In other terms, the requirement is that arg⁡(gt​(x))∈(π2,3​π2)\arg(g_{t}(x))\in(\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{3\pi}{2}) for all xx on cc with small |x||x|.

In case V∩Dt~=∅V\cap\widetilde{D_{t}}=\emptyset, we do not impose any condition on c⊗egtc\otimes e^{g_{t}}. Let 𝒞Xt~rd,−p​(e−gt){\mathcal{C}^{{\rm rd},-p}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}}(e^{-g_{t}}) denote the subsheaf of 𝒞Xt~,Dt~−p⊗egt\mathcal{C}_{\widetilde{X_{t}},\widetilde{D_{t}}}^{-p}\otimes e^{g_{t}} generated by all rapid decay pp-chains and all chains inside UtU_{t}. As for the sign notation, note that the dual exponential module is denoted by 𝒪​e−gt\mathcal{O}e^{-g_{t}} and admits egte^{g_{t}} as holomorphic solution. Together with the usual boundary operator of chains, these give the complex of rapid decay chains 𝒞Xt~rd(e−gt):=(𝒞Xt~rd,−⋅(e−gt),∂){\mathcal{C}^{\rm rd}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}}(e^{-g_{t}}):=({\mathcal{C}^{{\rm rd},-\raisebox{-0.90417pt}{\mbox{\boldmath$\cdot$}}}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}}(e^{-g_{t}}),\partial).

Definition 2.2.

The rapid decay homology of 𝒪​e−gt\mathcal{O}e^{-g_{t}} is the hypercohomology

Hkr​d​(Ut,e−gt):=ℍ−k​(Xt~,𝒞Xt~rd​(e−gt)),H^{rd}_{k}(U_{t},e^{-g_{t}}):={\mathbb{H}}^{-k}(\widetilde{X_{t}},{\mathcal{C}^{\rm rd}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}}(e^{-g_{t}}))\ ,

where π:Xt~→Xtan\pi:\widetilde{X_{t}}\to X_{t}^{\rm an} denotes the oriented real blow-up of the normal crossing divisor Dt:=Xt∖UtD_{t}:=X_{t}\smallsetminus U_{t}.

In the same way as in [5], Prop. 3.10, one proves that this definition does not depend on the choice of the compactification XtX_{t}. We will comment on this later.

The usual barycentric subdivision operator on 𝒞Xt~,Dt~\mathcal{C}_{\widetilde{X_{t}},\widetilde{D_{t}}} induces a subdivision operator on the rapid decay complex. The latter is therefore easily seen to be a homotopically fine complex of sheaves (cp. [18], p. 87). Hence, the rapid decay homology can be computed as the cohomology of the cooresponding complex of global sections:

Hkr​d​(Ut,e−gt)=H−k​(Γ⁡(Xt~,𝒞Xt~rd​(e−gt))).H^{rd}_{k}(U_{t},e^{-g_{t}})=H^{-k}\left(\Gamma(\widetilde{X_{t}},{\mathcal{C}^{\rm rd}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}}(e^{-g_{t}}))\right)\ .

In other words, we can regard the elements of this group as relative topological cycles cc in Hk​(Xt,Dt,ℂ)H^{k}(X_{t},D_{t},\mathbb{C}) which satisfy the rapid decay condition for gtg_{t}.

Since UtU_{t} is assumed to be affine, the de Rham cohomology of 𝒪Ut​egt\mathcal{O}_{U_{t}}e^{g_{t}} can also be computed on the level of global sections

Hd​Rp​(Ut,egt):=ℍp​(Ut,(ΩUt|k⋅,∇t))≅Hp​(…→ΓUt​(ΩUt|kq)→∇tΓUt​(ΩUt|kq+1)→…),H_{dR}^{p}(U_{t},e^{g_{t}}):={\mathbb{H}}^{p}(U_{t},(\Omega_{U_{t}|k}^{\raisebox{-0.90417pt}{\mbox{\boldmath$\cdot$}}},\nabla_{t}))\cong H^{p}(\ldots\to\Gamma_{U_{t}}(\Omega_{U_{t}|k}^{q})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nabla_{t}}}{{\to}}\Gamma_{U_{t}}(\Omega_{U_{t}|k}^{q+1})\to\ldots)\ ,

with ∇t(ω)=d​ω+d​gt∧ω\nabla_{t}(\omega)=d\omega+dg_{t}\wedge\omega for a local section ω\omega of ΩUt|kq\Omega_{U_{t}|k}^{q}.

Now, if we have a global rapid decay chain c⊗egt∈Γ⁡(Xt~,𝒞prd​(e−gt))c\otimes e^{g_{t}}\in\Gamma(\widetilde{X_{t}},\mathcal{C}^{\rm rd}_{p}(e^{-g_{t}})) with respect to the dual bundle 𝒪Ut​e−gt\mathcal{O}_{U_{t}}e^{-g_{t}} and a meromorphic pp-form ω\omega, then the integral ∫cω​egt\int_{c}\omega e^{g_{t}} converges because the rapid decay of egte^{g_{t}} along cc annihilates the moderate growth of the meromorphic ω\omega. Let cτc_{\tau} denote the topological chain one gets by cutting off a small tubular neighborhood with radius τ\tau around the boundary ∂Δp\partial\Delta^{p} from the given topological chain cc. Then, for c⊗egt∈𝒞prd​(e−gt)​(Xt~)c\otimes e^{g_{t}}\in\mathcal{C}^{\rm rd}_{p}(e^{-g_{t}})(\widetilde{X_{t}}) and η∈Ωp−1(∗Dt)\eta\in\Omega^{p-1}(\ast D_{t}) a meromorphic (p−1)(p-1)-form, we have the ’limit Stokes formula’

∫c(∇tη)​egt=limτ→0∫cτ(∇tη)​egt=limτ→0∫∂cτη​egt=∫∂c−Dtη​egt\int\limits_{c}(\nabla_{t}\eta)e^{g_{t}}=\lim_{\tau\to 0}\int\limits_{c_{\tau}}(\nabla_{t}\eta)e^{g_{t}}=\lim_{\tau\to 0}\int\limits_{\partial c_{\tau}}\eta\,e^{g_{t}}=\int\limits_{\partial c-D_{t}}\eta\,e^{g_{t}}\,

where in the last step we used that by the given growth/decay conditions the integral over the faces of ∂cτ\partial c_{\tau} ’converging’ against the faces of ∂c\partial c contained in DtD_{t} vanishes.

The limit Stokes formula easily shows in the standard way that integrating a closed differential form over a given rd-cycle (i.e. with vanishing boundary value) only depends on the de Rham class of the differential form and the rd-homology class of the cycle. Thus, we have:

Proposition 2.3.

Integration induces a well defined bilinear pairing

(2.1) Hd​Rp​(Ut,egt)×Hpr​d​(Ut,e−gt)⟶ℂ,([ω],[c⊗egt])↦∫cω​egt,H^{p}_{dR}(U_{t},e^{g_{t}})\times H^{rd}_{p}(U_{t},e^{-g_{t}})\longrightarrow{\mathbb{C}}\ ,\ ([\omega],[c\otimes e^{g_{t}}])\mapsto\int\limits_{c}\omega\,e^{g_{t}}\ ,

which we call the period pairing of 𝒪Ut​egt\mathcal{O}_{U_{t}}e^{g_{t}}.

2.2. Duality

We will now prove the following duality theorem for the connection 𝒪Ut​egt\mathcal{O}_{U_{t}}e^{g_{t}} in arbitrary dimension dimUt\dim U_{t}.

Theorem 2.4.

The period pairing (2.1) is a perfect pairing of finite dimensional vector spaces.

Note that one has the analogous result for any connection (E,∇)(E,\nabla) with good formal structure in dimension dimUt≤2\dim U_{t}\leq 2 ([5], or [1] for dimUt=1\dim U_{t}=1 resp.). The proof given in the following is a generalization of the one in [5] for the special case of a connection 𝒪Ut​egt\mathcal{O}_{U_{t}}e^{g_{t}} to arbitrary dimension dim(Xt)∈ℕ\dim(X_{t})\in{\mathbb{N}}. For the readers’s convenience, we give the outline of the proof and also comment on the necessary changes for higher dimensions.

Proof.

The proof will rely on a local duality on Xt~\widetilde{X_{t}}. To prepare for it, we will describe the period pairing as a local pairing of complexes of sheaves on Xt~\widetilde{X_{t}}. We recall the corresponding notions of [5].

Let 𝒜Xt~mod​Dt\mathcal{A}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{{\rm mod}D_{t}} denote the sheaf of functions on Xt~\widetilde{X_{t}} which are holomorphic on Utan⊂Xt~U_{t}^{\rm an}\subset\widetilde{X_{t}} and of moderate growth along π−1​(Dt)\pi^{-1}(D_{t}) and let 𝒜Xt~<Dt\mathcal{A}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{<D_{t}} denote the subsheaf of such functions that are infinitely flat along Dt~\widetilde{D_{t}}, i.e. all of whose partial derivatives of arbitrary order vanish on Dt~\widetilde{D_{t}}.

These sheaves are both flat over π−1​(𝒪Xt)\pi^{-1}(\mathcal{O}_{X_{t}}) and we call

DRXt~mod​Dt(egt):=𝒜Xt~mod​Dt⊗π−1​(𝒪Xt)π−1(DRXtan(𝒪Xt[∗Dt]egt)){\rm DR}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{{\rm mod}D_{t}}(e^{g_{t}}):=\mathcal{A}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{{\rm mod}D_{t}}\otimes_{\pi^{-1}(\mathcal{O}_{X_{t}})}\pi^{-1}({\rm DR}_{X_{t}^{\rm an}}(\mathcal{O}_{X_{t}}[\ast D_{t}]e^{g_{t}}))

the moderate de Rham complex of 𝒪Ut​egt\mathcal{O}_{U_{t}}e^{g_{t}} and

DRXt~<Dt(egt):=𝒜Xt~<Dt⊗π−1​(𝒪Xt)π−1(DRXtan(𝒪Xt[∗Dt]egt)){\rm DR}^{<D_{t}}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}(e^{g_{t}}):=\mathcal{A}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{<D_{t}}\otimes_{\pi^{-1}(\mathcal{O}_{X_{t}})}\pi^{-1}({\rm DR}_{X_{t}^{\rm an}}(\mathcal{O}_{X_{t}}[\ast D_{t}]e^{g_{t}}))

the asymptotically flat de Rham complex. Note that the first one computes the meromorphic de Rham cohomology of the meromorphic connection 𝒪Xt[∗Dt]egt\mathcal{O}_{X_{t}}[\ast D_{t}]e^{g_{t}} (cp. [15], Corollaire 1.1.8).

Now, the wedge product obviously defines a pairing of complexes of sheaves on Xt~\widetilde{X_{t}}:

(2.2) DRXt~mod​Dt​(egt)⊗ℂDRXt~<Dt​(e−gt)→DRXt~<Dt​(𝒪Xt,d),{\rm DR}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{{\rm mod}D_{t}}(e^{g_{t}})\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}{\rm DR}^{<D_{t}}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}(e^{-g_{t}})\to{\rm DR}^{<D_{t}}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}(\mathcal{O}_{X_{t}},d)\ ,

where the right hand side denotes the asymptotically flat de Rham complex of the trivial connection. We will compare this pairing to the periods pairing from above.

Before that, let us introduce the sheaf 𝔇​𝔟Xt~rd,−s\mathfrak{Db}_{\widetilde{X_{t}}}^{{\rm rd},-s} of rapid decay distributions on Xt~\widetilde{X_{t}}, the local section of which are distributions

We will now study the exponential Gauß-Manin systems and apply these considerations to describe the holomorphic solutions of the latter.

3. Holomorphic solutions of exponential Gauß-Manin systems

Consider the situation described in the introduction. Let f,g:U→𝔸1f,g:U\to\mathbb{A}^{1} be two algebraically independant regular functions on the smooth affine variety UU. We denote by XX a smooth projective compactification of UU, on which f,g:U→𝔸1f,g:U\to\mathbb{A}^{1} extend to functions F,G:X→ℙ1F,G:X\to\mathbb{P}^{1}. Let D:=X∖UD:=X\setminus U and assume that it is a normal crossing divisor.

3.1. Definition

We define an exponential Gauß-Manin systems as being the cohomology sheaves of the direct image by ff of the module of exponential type 𝒪U​eg\mathcal{O}_{U}e^{g}:

𝒢k:=ℋk​f+​(𝒪U​eg).\mathcal{G}^{k}:=\mathcal{H}^{k}f_{+}(\mathcal{O}_{U}e^{g}).

Let ΩUk\Omega_{U}^{k} be the sheaf of algebraic differential forms of degree kk on UU. Using the canonical factorisation of ff into a closed embedding and a projection, we prove as in [4] that:

Proposition 3.1.

f+​(𝒪U​eg)f_{+}(\mathcal{O}_{U}e^{g}) is isomorphic to f∗(ΩU∙+n⊗ℂℂ[∂t])f_{\ast}(\Omega_{U}^{\bullet+n}\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}[\partial_{t}]), where the differential ∇\nabla on ΩU∙+n⊗ℂℂ[∂t]\Omega_{U}^{\bullet+n}\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}[\partial_{t}] is given by

∇(w⊗∂ti)=dw⊗∂ti+dg∧w⊗∂ti−df∧w⊗∂ti+1.\nabla(w\otimes\partial_{t}^{i})=dw\otimes\partial_{t}^{i}+dg\wedge w\otimes\partial_{t}^{i}-df\wedge w\otimes\partial_{t}^{i+1}.

Its cohomology modules 𝒢k\mathcal{G}^{k} are equipped with a structure of 𝒟𝔸1\mathcal{D}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}-module given by:

t[w∂ti]=[fw∂ti−iw∂ti−1],∂t[w∂ti]=[w∂ti+1].\begin{array}[]{l}t[w\partial_{t}^{i}]=[fw\partial_{t}^{i}-iw\partial_{t}^{i-1}],\\ \partial_{t}[w\partial_{t}^{i}]=[w\partial_{t}^{i+1}].\end{array}

They are holonomic 𝒟𝔸1\mathcal{D}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}-modules with irregular singularities on the affine line 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1} and at infinity.

Remark 3.2.

The interpretation of the regular singularities of 𝒢k\mathcal{G}^{k} in terms of invariants associated to ff and gg is still unknown. Nevertheless, in [13] and [14], a complete description of the irregular singularities is given. Let Δk⊂𝔸1×𝔸1\Delta_{k}\subset\mathbb{A}^{1}\times\mathbb{A}^{1} be the singular support of the holonomic 𝒟𝔸1×𝔸1\mathcal{D}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}}-module ℋk​(f,g)+​(𝒪U)\mathcal{H}^{k}(f,g)_{+}(\mathcal{O}_{U}). Its closure Δk¯\overline{\Delta_{k}} in ℙ1×ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1}\times\mathbb{P}^{1} is included in the projective variety Δ¯\overline{\Delta}, such that (F,G):(F,G)−1​((ℙ1×ℙ1)∖Δ¯)→(ℙ1×ℙ1)∖Δ¯(F,G):(F,G)^{-1}((\mathbb{P}^{1}\times\mathbb{P}^{1})\setminus\overline{\Delta})\to(\mathbb{P}^{1}\times\mathbb{P}^{1})\setminus\overline{\Delta} is a locally trivial fibration. t0∈𝔸1∪{∞}t_{0}\in\mathbb{A}^{1}\cup\{\infty\} is an irregular singularity of 𝒢k\mathcal{G}^{k} if and only if the germ of Δk¯\overline{\Delta_{k}} at (t0,∞)(t_{0},\infty) is not empty and not included in {t0}×ℙ1\{t_{0}\}\times\mathbb{P}^{1}.

3.2. Results on the exponential Gauß-Manin systems

Proposition 3.5.

There exists a finite subset Σ2\Sigma_{2} of ℂ\mathbb{C} such that

Let 𝒲\mathcal{W} be a Whitney stratification of XX such that G−1​(∞)G^{-1}(\infty), DD and UU are union of strata (cf. Theorem (2.2) in [20]). The central argument of this proof is the following lemma.

Lemma 3.6.

There exists a finite subset Σ2\Sigma_{2} of ℂ\mathbb{C} such that F:F−1​(ℂ∖Σ2)→ℂ∖Σ2F:F^{-1}(\mathbb{C}\setminus\Sigma_{2})\to\mathbb{C}\setminus\Sigma_{2} is a locally trivial fibration which respect the stratification on F−1​(ℂ∖Σ2)F^{-1}(\mathbb{C}\setminus\Sigma_{2}) induced by 𝒲\mathcal{W}.
